title: Qur'anic iltifāt: expanded catalogue of grammatical-person shifts
scope: All 326 unique candidates in the supplied catalogue.json, corresponding to Abdel Haleem's four person-shift lists. This is a source-based catalogue, not an exhaustive census of every possible Qur'anic iltifāt. The separate 36:22 candidate from the earlier file is outside the supplied list and is not added here.
method: Every input candidate is retained once, in the original directions, after comparison with the scholarly lists and review of verse text and nearby context. The inclusive ayah_from–ayah_to range contains relevant context and the identified turn; it need not locate a unique adjacent pair. A source anchor may occur before or after the actual turn, and the verse_url retains that input anchor. Explanations are editorial contextual interpretations informed by the cited scholarly classification, not quotations or claims of verse-specific scholarly commentary. Grammatical person describes the referent being spoken about, addressed, or speaking; first-person forms can belong to humans in quoted speech rather than to God. Candidates with explicit speech-boundary or referent-identity concerns are flagged disputed. This flag denotes editorial classification reservations here, not evidence that named scholars disagree about every flagged verse.
source_notes: The supplied catalogue contains no citations or explanations; its 326 references and directions match the four lists in the accessible reproduction of Abdel Haleem (1992). The original study calls its lists non-final. Apparent source-anchor problems are handled with contextual ranges: the first-person verb for 86:15 is in 86:16, and the third-person name for the first-to-third entry anchored at 87:6 is in 87:7. The first-person voice already begins before the anchors 32:27 and 52:21. The second-to-third entry at 2:216 and several changes involving different groups or explicit quotations require particular caution. Ranges sharing a passage can represent different directional candidates; counts are candidate records, not distinct verses or a definitive count of rhetorical events. Arabic checks use the Hafs text; this catalogue does not survey variant readings.

person_values.third: one spoken about (he/she/they or a name/title)

status_values.well_attested: Present in the scholarly list, with a person alternation identifiable in the stated context; does not mean unanimous classification or a proven exclusive rhetorical purpose.
status_values.disputed: Retained source-listed candidate with an editorial concern about identical referent, speech boundary, or locating the claimed direction. The reason explains that concern; no scholarly dispute is implied without supporting attribution.

abdel_haleem_1992.author: M. A. S. Abdel Haleem
abdel_haleem_1992.title: Grammatical Shift for Rhetorical Purposes: Iltifāt and Related Features in the Qur'ān
abdel_haleem_1992.publication: Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 55, no. 3 (1992): 407–432
